the isolation and purification of soluble tumorassociated and embryonic cell surface antigens from the DMH‐BU1 colon carcinoma and the characterization of these antigens by their ability to inhibit LNC‐mediatcd cytotoxicity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the soluble intracytoplasmatic protein fractions of the DMH‐BU1 colon carcinoma contain antigens which are common to all rat colon carcinomas and are not embryonic antigens.
soluble fractions of a rat colon carcinoma possess both tumor‐associated antigens (TAA) and embryonic antigans (EA).
the soluble preparations of DMH‐BU‐1 contain common tumorassociated antigens and embryonic antigengenetic determinants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that a single fraction of a chemically induced tumor contains antigens which are both embryonic and tumor‐associated.
we have been able to separate a fraction of the tumor‐associated antigen (TAA) from the EA and that the EA can be further separated into at least 2 components.
